readings: Join laboratory test records to patients by patient ID and group all matched records by patient sex, treating a missing sex as an unknown-sex group. Compute the average record count across those groups. For each group above that average, show the sex or unknown-sex label, its record count, its share of all matched records, and the unrounded amount by which its count exceeds the average.

Join laboratory test records to patients by patient ID and exclude records whose patient sex is missing. Group the remaining records by sex and compute the average record count across those sexes. For each sex above that average, show the sex, its record count, its share of all matched records with known patient sex, and the unrounded amount by which its count exceeds the average.
queries:
WITH sex_counts AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(p.SEX), ''), 'Unknown') AS sex,
           COUNT(*) AS record_count
    FROM Laboratory AS l
    JOIN Patient AS p ON p.ID = l.ID
    GROUP BY COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(p.SEX), ''), 'Unknown')
),
stats AS (
    SELECT AVG(record_count) AS average_count,
           SUM(record_count) AS total_count
    FROM sex_counts
)
SELECT s.sex,
       s.record_count,
       1.0 * s.record_count / stats.total_count AS share,
       s.record_count - stats.average_count AS amount_above_average
FROM sex_counts AS s
CROSS JOIN stats
WHERE s.record_count > stats.average_count;

WITH sex_counts AS (
    SELECT p.SEX AS sex, COUNT(*) AS record_count
    FROM Laboratory AS l
    JOIN Patient AS p ON p.ID = l.ID
    WHERE p.SEX IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY p.SEX
),
totals AS (
    SELECT AVG(record_count) AS average_count,
           SUM(record_count) AS total_count
    FROM sex_counts
)
SELECT s.sex,
       s.record_count,
       1.0 * s.record_count / t.total_count AS record_share,
       s.record_count - t.average_count AS amount_above_average
FROM sex_counts AS s
CROSS JOIN totals AS t
WHERE s.record_count > t.average_count
